subject: Argenta Health — private connectivity readiness & install sequencing
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@argentahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Seth Cole <seth.cole@argentahealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment connectivity & sequencing questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're starting to lock down the network and maintenance windows for our private deployment with Redwood. A few high-level constraints and notes from our side up front so the implementation team can scope the work: 

- We have an on-prem datacenter segment (10.10.0.0/16) that must remain air-gapped for PHI processing; any connections will flow through our transit gateway.
- Primary cloud VPC (us-west-2) has 172.31.0.0/16; we want VPC peering (transit) to handle model traffic, and private endpoints for control-plane API calls.
- We use AWS TGW, BGP to on-prem via Direct Connect (ASN 64512).
- TLS termination for inbound connections should remain on our side; Redwood should support mTLS to the private endpoint.

I've attached the initial network inventory and a rough diagram. Can the Redwood team confirm the following items before we schedule the three-hour maintenance window next month?

1) Required public/private IP ranges Redwood will need reserved (e.g., for private endpoint ENIs).
2) Whether Redwood requires any specific route tables/NAT behavior inside our VPCs.
3) Expected open ports (control & data) — note we restrict everything to explicit allow lists.
4) HSM/KeyWrap assumptions for KMS integration — we'll need to surface our compliance constraints.

Attachments: [attachment: argenta_vpc_inventory.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [attachment: argenta_network_diagram.v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Best,
Lina Park
Director, IT Infrastructure
Argenta Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@argentahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity & sequencing questions

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Marcus (network/ops), Karthik (deploy lead), and Grace (security/compliance) so we can collect technical answers and a recommended sequencing.

Quick responses to your four asks below; we'll follow up with a short runbook and a proposed three-hour maintenance window slot.

1) IP ranges: Redwood's private endpoint model uses ENIs in your VPC. We request you reserve two /28 subnets in the same AZs you plan to host the workload (one for control-plane ENIs, one for data egress). If you prefer to avoid ENIs we can instead publish an interface endpoint — we'll confirm during the network review.

2) Route tables/NAT: For our typical setup we ask that subnets with ENIs have routes to the TGW and that outbound model traffic be allowed to Redwood's egress CIDR (we'll provide this). If your VPC uses centralized NAT gateways, we'll need a route so KV cache traffic can reach our egress.

3) Ports: Control-plane (HTTPS/mTLS) 443; data-plane depends on model options but usually TCP 443 as well. If you use internal-only IPs we prefer mTLS on the control channel and an allowlist by ENI IP.

4) KMS/HSM: Grace — can you confirm if Redwood's standard KMS integration pattern (customer-managed keys with envelope encryption) passes Argenta's compliance needs, or if we should plan HSM keywrap options for on-prem?

Next steps I propose:
- Technical review call (60m): Marcus, Karthik, Argenta network ops (Lina + Seth) — to validate subnets, BGP, and route propagation.
- Security sync (30m): Grace + Argenta security to confirm KMS/HSM expectations and audit logging.
- Delivery runbook (we'll send): sequencing, fallback, and rollback steps.

Proposed times (PST): Tue 2025-11-11 09:00, Tue 11:00, or Wed 2025-11-12 14:00. Which works?

I'll attach our private-deploy preflight checklist for review.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-private-deploy-preflight-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-06T08:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity & sequencing questions

Tessa / team — I've reviewed the Argenta diagram and inventory. Notes for the technical review call: 

- ENI vs Interface Endpoint: If Argenta prefers no ENIs in customer subnets, we can use AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). That avoids needing reserved /28s but requires specific security group rules and endpoint service acceptance on their side.
- TGW & BGP: Because they use BGP over DX, confirm we get propagated routes for the ENI prefixes. We'll register the ENI IP ranges with TGW route tables and ensure BGP advertisements include those CIDRs.
- NAT behavior: If their subnets route outbound through a centralized NAT, we need to validate SNAT policy; long-lived connections from the models (KV cache) can be disrupted by aggressive ephemeral SNAT. Recommend they allocate NAT with consistent source IPs for egress to our service.
- Ports: 443 mTLS for control. For data plane, if they want to avoid egress entirely, we can deploy an on-prem appliance (appliance package) that terminates traffic locally and syncs model weights via a secured push. That would add an installation step but reduces exposure.
- HSM: If Argenta's auditors require HSM-backed keywrap for KMS, we have a path to support external HSM via customer-managed CloudHSM or an on-prem HSM wrap step in the appliance install. Grace, we'll need your input on the minimum audit logs we must ship to meet SOC2 + healthcare PII audit traces.

I'll prepare a short list of specific firewall rules and the ENI CIDR ranges we'll request for the call.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Park <lina.park@argentahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Seth Cole <seth.cole@argentahealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-07T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity & sequencing questions

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping the technical team. Tue 2025-11-11 at 09:00 PST works for our network leads.

Answers / items we can provide before the call:
- Reserved space: we can carve two /28s in us-west-2a and us-west-2b for the ENIs. I'll upload a cleaned diagram with subnet IDs.
- TGW/BGP: ASN 64512 is already established; we'll ensure route propagation includes the ENI prefixes.
- NAT: we can provide a NAT gateway with consistent elastic IPs for egress to Redwood if needed.
- HSM: Argenta currently uses an on-prem Luna HSM for key wrapping. We are open to CloudHSM if Redwood requires it, but auditors prefer HSM-backed keywrap and full-key lifecycle logs.

Attachments: [attachment: argenta_network_diagram.v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
Link to our intake ticket: https://argenta.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9192

See you on Tue. We'll include our security lead (cc'd) if needed.

Best,
Lina
